source: Letter-associates cross-reference — Alexander's company circle vs. the 60th NY record
method: Read all 28 letters linked to Alexander; extracted every named comrade/officer; cross-referenced each against the NY AG 60th NY roster and Richard Eddy's 1864 regimental history. Names tied to other units (Henry's 34th NY, Charles's 153rd NY) or to home/academy life were recorded as honest NULLs for the 60th — never forced into a match. This mirrors the Henry Sweep 1.1 company-circle method.
anchor_record: HUBBELL, ALEXANDER F.—Age 18; enlisted Sept 21 1861 at Champlain; corporal Co. H Oct 30 1861; sergeant Oct 1 1862; veteran Dec 14 1863; mustered out July 17 1865, Alexandria, Va. (Eddy lists him in the Co. H roll AND the Lookout Mountain wounded list.)

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: Capt. Ransom (signs 'James H. Ransom'; letters vary J.B./J.H.)
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'Capt. Ransom took tea with us' (1862-10-02); writes Mother directly, signed 'James H. Ransom' (1863-01-14); 'The men of Capt. Ransom's Co. complain that he took home... his Co.'s money' (1863-03-12).
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: RANSOM, JAMES M.—Age 33; enrolled Sept 21 1861 at Ogdensburg; captain Co. H Oct 17 1861; discharged Feb 2 1863. Eddy: elected Captain of the Champlain/Mooers/Chazy company.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: Alexander's company commander; the family hosted him at home. Middle initial in letters (J.B./J.H.) differs from record (M.) — same man (James M. Ransom of Champlain).

confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: (Alexander's lieutenant; the NCO promotion chain in his letters runs through the Co. H officers.)
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: WHITE, LORING E.—Age 22; first lieutenant Co. H Oct 30 1861; died of typhoid fever July 26 1862 at Little Washington, Va.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: FATE RECOVERED — a death the letters never report; opened the lieutenant vacancy Fitch filled.

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: (orderly sergeant) → 'when their orderly is promoted to Lieut.' = Charles H. Dickinson
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'he is now third sergeant and when their orderly is promoted to Lieut. he will be second sergeant'
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: DICKINSON, CHARLES H.—Age 25; first (orderly) sergeant Co. H Oct 30 1861; second lieutenant July 26 1862; discharged Nov 30 1862, Falmouth, Va.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: The 'orderly' whose promotion drove the NCO chain Alexander rose through. Binds the letters' promotion talk to the record exactly.

confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'your friend, Amos C. Luther' (writes Alexander, 1862-10-12); 'sergeant Howes and Luther were the singers' in Alex's tent (1863-03-12).
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: LUTHER, AMOS G.—Age 18; corporal Co. H Oct 30 1861 (enrolled Oct 19 at Chazy); sergeant July 1 1863; veteran Dec 11 1863; first sergeant Sept 1 1864; mustered out July 17 1865; commissioned (not mustered) 2nd Lt. July 5 1865.
confirmed_co_H_associates.fate_from_record: survived; rose to first sergeant; commissioned 2nd Lt. (not mustered)
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: Alexander's closest comrade in the letters (the muster roll M01 already paired them). Middle initial C. (letters) vs G. (record) — same man.

confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: 'Commissary Howes came in (he rooms with me)' (1862-02-17); 'sergeant Howes... the singers' in Alex's tent (1863-03-12).
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: HOWES, ALVAH S.—Age 21; enlisted Sept 21 1861 at Ellenburg; wagoner Co. H Oct 30 1861; later private/sergeant; veteran Dec 14 1863; mustered out July 31 1865, Ogdensburg.

confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: (Co. H NCO line; named in the disambiguation watch-list.)
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: BROCKWAY, PATRICK H.—Age 21; sergeant Co. H Oct 30 1861; first sergeant Nov 20 1862; veteran Dec 14 1863; first lieutenant Co. C Aug 12 1864; captain Co. H Mar 29 1865; mustered out July 17 1865.
confirmed_co_H_associates.fate_from_record: survived; ended the war as Co. H's captain
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: The Co. H NCO who rose to command the company by war's end.

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: Sidney Rider (beside Hubbell in the Lookout Mountain casualty list)
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: (Eddy lists 'Private Sidney Rider, Co. H' immediately before 'Sergeant A. F. Hubbell' in the wounded list.)
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: RIDER, SIDNEY—Age 18; enlisted Sept 21 1861 at Champlain; private Co. H; mustered out Oct 29 1864.
confirmed_co_H_associates.fate_from_record: wounded at Lookout Mountain with Alexander; mustered out 1864
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: Same-day, same-place (Champlain) enlistee; wounded alongside Alexander — the exact comrade-binding move that worked for Henry (Jolly beside Hubbell).

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: Alexander Lablue ('belongs to Capt. Ransom's Company')
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: (named in R. W. McDonald's letter as a Capt. Ransom's-company man; Eddy Co. H roll 'Lablue, A.')
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: LABLUE, ALEXANDER—Age 18; enlisted Sept 21 1861 at Champlain; private Co. H; deserted Oct 24 1862 from Loudon Heights, Va.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: FATE RECOVERED — desertion the family letters never mention.

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: Edwin H. Porter (Eddy: 'Death of E. H. Porter')
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: Tangled with the family's 'Capt. Ransom had a narrow escape' railroad story (Dec 1861).
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: PORTER, EDWIN H.—Age 23; enlisted Sept 21 1861 at Bloomingdale; private Co. H; accidentally killed by the cars, Jan 8 1862, near Baltimore, Md.
confirmed_co_H_associates.fate_from_record: accidentally killed by railroad cars, Jan 8 1862
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: FATE RECOVERED — the documented Co. H railroad death near Baltimore, echoing the letters' 'narrow escape' anecdote.

confirmed_co_H_associates.name_as_written: James E. White (possible 'poisoned man'? — not confirmable)
confirmed_co_H_associates.verbatim_letter_context: Alexander reported a man poisoned (Feb 1862) — identification with this White is NOT confirmable.
confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: WHITE, JAMES E.—Age 18; enlisted Sept 27 1861 at Ellensburg; private Co. H; wounded; died of wounds Aug 28 1862, Washington, D.C.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: Documented Co. H death; the poisoning link is flagged as unconfirmed, not forced.

confirmed_co_H_associates.record_match: Eddy Co. H org roll lists 'Malhinch, T.'; no clean AG roster line under Malhinch/Nelhinch.
confirmed_co_H_associates.note: Partial/probable match (handwritten-name transcription); reported honestly, not forced.

regimental_loss.name: Col. William B. Goodrich (Mother's 'the 60th Regt. has lost its Col.')
regimental_loss.record_match: Eddy (Gen. Greene's official letter): 'The death of Colonel Goodrich by the hands of the insurgents, whilst gallantly leading my Brigade into action, at the battle of Antietam...' Eddy: 'he gently, and without pain, passed from life.'
regimental_loss.note: The regimental loss Mother read of in Sept 1862 — corroborated and named in the record.
